acceptance_criteria: A interaction partial R-squared at least 0.005
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared above 0 on expiry-window holdout rows
Net daily edge after the 0.10% round-trip taker cost is positive
spec.alternative_hypothesis: The lag-1 BTC coefficient for next-day ETH returns is larger inside expiry windows than outside them (positive interaction), and lag-1 BTC explains a positive out-of-sample component of next-day ETH returns within expiry-window rows.
spec.benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-bar ETH return predicted from its own lagged return, the SOL common factor and lag-1 BTC, with the interaction excluded
cost_assumptions: OKX VIP0 taker fee 0.05% per side, from the OKX public fee schedule (okx.com/fees), checked 2026-11-18; treated as an assumption, not verified for the user's account
Funding rate costs ignored; perpetual funding can exceed taker fees over holding periods
Slippage and market impact ignored; both would reduce any edge
spec.cost_model: Round-trip taker cost 0.10% per position flip (OKX VIP0 taker 0.05% per side, assumed); sign rule on out-of-sample augmented forecasts on expiry-window holdout rows only, 1x, flat on non-window rows; entry from flat and final exit cost one taker side each; funding, slippage and market impact ignored
exclusions: Unconfirmed (forming) OKX bars are excluded; only confirm=1 candles enter the panel
The first daily return row has no lag-1 predictor and is excluded; the same warm-up rule applies to the 1H panel
Bars after the preregistered window end 2026-11-18T16:00Z are out of sample
known_confounders: The expiry window is only a proxy for dealer-hedging intensity; Deribit public data gives whole-market OI and Greeks, not dealer positions, so dealer gamma exposure cannot be verified

In crypto, forced buying and selling are dominated by perpetual liquidations, open interest and funding rates; options gamma is only an environment variable, so a window effect must not be default-attributed to gamma
Monthly expiries are scarce (about 12 per year); the daily window sample is roughly 280 rows of about 2,100, so power against small effects is limited
The SOL common-factor proxy is itself driven by BTC and may absorb part of the transmission effect; no-factor controls are reported as upper bounds
Common crypto market shocks move BTC, ETH and SOL together; the regressions control for the contemporaneous third-asset return only
The T-day daily return spans the Friday 08:00 UTC settlement (bars open 16:00 UTC); the T-1 bar's interval contains the settlement moment and the T bar is the first full post-settlement bar
spec.mechanism: Expiry-related position management (dealer hedging, position closing and repositioning around settlement) may concentrate information flow in the days before expiry, so price discovery in the largest market (BTC perpetuals) transmits to ETH with a stronger lag inside the window. The expiry window is only a proxy for dealer-hedging intensity, not a measurement of it. Deribit public data reports whole-market per-contract open interest and Greeks, not dealer positions, so dealer net gamma, dealer positions and hedging flow cannot be verified from public data. This study tests the expiry-window effect itself; any hedging interpretation is inference, not observation. In crypto, forced buying and selling are dominated by perpetual liquidations, open interest and funding rates, and options gamma is only an environment variable.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count
model_definition: Interaction OLS with HAC standard errors (daily BTC→ETH, 1H BTC→ETH)
Expiry-window-subsample partial lead-lag with HAC standard errors
Window-aware purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation (expiry-window holdout rows only)
Wide-window (T-5..T+1), quarterly-vs-monthly and subperiod splits as descriptive checks (not in the test family)
DVOL around expiry as a descriptive check (not in the test family)
spec.multiple_testing_family: Expiry-window BTC→ETH daily transmission (3 tests: A daily interaction, B daily expiry-window subsample, C 1H interaction)
spec.null_hypothesis: Lag-1 BTC returns have no expiry-window-dependent incremental predictive value: the interaction coefficient is zero and lag-1 BTC does not predict ETH returns within expiry-window rows, beyond ETH's own history and the common-factor control, after costs and dependence controls.
spec.primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the BTC×expiry-window interaction in the daily BTC→ETH interaction regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted A interaction p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0 on expiry-window holdout rows
Net daily edge after costs is zero or negative
spec.research_question: Does lag-1 BTC perpetual return predict the next-day ETH perpetual return more strongly inside Deribit monthly option expiry windows (bar-open dates T-3..T, T the last Friday of the month, settlement 08:00 UTC) than outside them?
spec.target_definition: Next-day close-to-close ETH-USDT perpetual log return (daily primary); next-hour ETH-USDT perpetual log return (1H secondary)
spec.title: Expiry windows strengthen BTC→ETH transmission
